condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

Indicator 3: Preparation and submission of Jordan’s Fourth National Communication (4NC) and Second Biennial Update Report (2BUR) to the Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC as part of the fulfilment of its obligations to the Convention according to Articles 4 and 12, and subsequent Decisions 1/CP. 16 par. 60 and 2/CP. 17 par. 41 and its Annex III

comment.narrative:
Latest national circumstances chapter at all sectors for the baseline years 2012 was developed in the first BUR.
The First BUR inventories were estimated using the 2006, IPCC Guidelines whereas the previous inventory of the Third NC was estimated using the Revised 1996 IPCC Guidelines.
The GHG mitigation analysis within the previous NCs and BUR assessed potential human interventions that can be implemented at the national level to reduce anthropogenic emissions of GHGs in different sectors to support the overall global efforts to limit the magnitude and/or rate of long-term induced global warming.
It has been estimated that up to the year 2050, additional 5 billion US$ will be needed for adaptation, TNC identified barriers to adaptation to climate change as: • Lack of financial resources. • Climate change risks not sufficiently taken into account within sectoral policies and investment frameworks • Capacity building is needed specially in modeling
No fourth NC and Second BUR in Jordan

Submission of the Second Biennial Report by Dec 2019 and submission of the Fourth National Communication Report by Dec 2022. National circumstances and institutional arrangements relevant to the preparation of the NCs and BURs on continuous basis described and updated. Conduct a study on different gender roles in adaptation and mitigation interventions at the community level, policy formulation and decision-making process. GHG inventories for the years 2016 (Second BUR) and 2017 (Fourth NC) are estimated for sources and sinks for all sectors. Updating the Emission factors for the key sources for potential use of tier 2. The enhancement of capacity of participating agencies and cross-sector collaboration, through training on LEAP software.

Finalizing the submission of the Second Biennial Report by Dec 2019 and submission of the Fourth National Communication Report by Dec 2022. Finalizing national circumstances and institutional arrangements relevant to the preparation of the NCs and BURs on continuous basis described and updated. Initiating a study on different gender roles in adaptation and mitigation interventions at the community level, policy formulation and decision-making process. Finalizing GHG inventories for the years 2016 (Second BUR) and 2017 (Fourth NC) are estimated for sources and sinks for all sectors. Finalizing updating the Emission factors for the key sources for potential use of tier 2. Concluding the enhancement of capacity of participating agencies and cross-sector collaboration, through training on LEAP software.

- Validate and submit the Second Biennial Report (2BUR) to the UNFCCC - Initiate the process to update the Climate Change National Policy - Undertake climate change gender analysis to provide the Fourth National Communication Report (4NC) with informationan required to include gender perspectives in the climate change mitigation and adaptation - Prepare and validate the Naional Circumastances Chapter of the Fourth National Communication Report (4NC)

GHGs inventory by sector/by source was finalized and visualized to inform the climate change decision making process and define the needed mitigation measures for carbon cuts.
Barriers that hinder gender mainstreaming in climate cation in Jordan is well defined, opportunities to achieve gender equality in climate change agenda were highlighted and promoted among climate change concerned stakeholders
National circumstances on the main development sectors of water, agriculture, health, socio-economic and health on the baseline year of 2017 were documented and validated by all development sectors

- Finalize and endorse the national climate change policy - Undertake the climate change vulnerability assessment in the main development sectors of water, agriculture, health, socio-economic and urban to define the underlying causes of vulnerability for each sector - Undertake the mitigation analysis in the energy, transport, water and agriculture sectors - Prepare, finalize and submit the 4NC to the UNFCCC
